visual.general_description: Multi-series line chart of thyroid function and antibody values over gestational weeks and weeks after birth, with a stepped bar chart of methimazole dose underneath.
visual.detailed_description: A white-background chart with a legend across the top reading TSH mIU/L (blue line), fT4 pg/ml (orange line), fT3 pg/ml (grey line) and TRAb U/L (yellow line), each drawn as a smoothed line with round markers. Three vertical axes are printed: a left TSH mIU/L axis with ticks 0 to 5, an adjacent fT4-fT3 pg/ml axis with ticks 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30, and a right TRAb U/L axis with ticks 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50. The lower axis has a Gestational Weeks scale with ticks 10, 20, 30 and 40 and, to its right, a separate Weeks After Birth scale with ticks 0, 10 and 20. A dashed orange vertical line carries a boxed DELIVERY label above it and sits at the 40 mark of the gestational scale where the weeks-after-birth scale starts at 0. The blue TSH line stays at the zero baseline with round markers across the gestational weeks and for several markers after delivery, then rises steeply to a peak near the upper end of the TSH axis and falls to a lower marker at the right end. The orange fT4 line starts at its highest point near 27 on the fT4-fT3 axis at the left edge, falls over the first weeks and then fluctuates around the 10 to 16 range with small peaks, and stays near 10 to 15 after delivery. The grey fT3 line starts near 14 at the left edge, drops to about 5 and then drifts slowly down toward about 3 across the rest of the chart. The yellow TRAb line rises from about 17 on the right-hand axis, with a first plateau between the gestational weeks of 25 and 36, a second rise to its peak after delivery near the upper part of the TRAb axis, then falls to a low near 15 and rises again at the right end. Below the chart, a title reads Treatment MMI (mg) above a blue stepped bar chart whose steps are labelled 10, 15, 12,5, 10, 7,5, 10 and 15, rising at the left, stepping up and down across gestation and rising again at the far right. No panel letters, arrows, annotations beyond the DELIVERY label, names, dates or identifiers are visible.

pixel_observations: Legend at the top: TSH mIU/L (blue), fT4 pg/ml (orange), fT3 pg/ml (grey), TRAb U/L (yellow), all drawn as smoothed lines with round markers.
Three vertical axes are printed: TSH mIU/L with ticks 0 to 5 on the far left, fT4-fT3 pg/ml with ticks 0 to 30 in steps of 5, and TRAb U/L with ticks 0 to 50 in steps of 10 on the right.
Two horizontal scales are printed: Gestational Weeks with ticks 10, 20, 30, 40, and a separate Weeks After Birth scale with ticks 0, 10, 20.
A dashed orange vertical line with a boxed DELIVERY label sits at the 40 mark of the gestational scale where the weeks-after-birth scale begins.

The blue TSH line stays at the zero baseline across the gestational weeks and for some markers after delivery, then rises to a high peak and falls to a lower final marker; no numeric values are printed on the markers.

The orange fT4 line starts highest at the left edge (near 27 on its axis) and then falls and fluctuates; the grey fT3 line starts near 14 and falls to a low plateau; the yellow TRAb line rises through gestation, peaks after delivery, falls and rises again at the right end.
A bar chart titled Treatment MMI (mg) lies below the line chart; its steps carry the printed labels 10, 15, 12,5, 10, 7,5, 10 and 15 (comma decimal separators as printed).
The postpartum markers are positioned on the weeks-after-birth scale (last marker near 21 on that scale), while the source table labels postpartum rows in months; the two are not reconciled here.
